visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. Built from components/site/v3. Same place-type class as /cities/[slug]/types/[type].
competitiveTarget: Beat Zillow / Redfin community type filters. A dedicated community+type page with leftover/segment stats, the parent community atlas, and photographed listings of that type, instead of a search-results URL. Unique title, canonical, ItemList when listings exist. Breadcrumb is City then type, no Home.
note: Same composition as /cities/[slug]/types/[type], from that route's _v3 components plus this route's PlaceTypeFilm (shadcn-carousel import on the community _v3). H1 `{Type} in {Place}` is the only display line; the Atlas wears an eyebrow under it; one section-0 claim sentence with its source line, single-sourced on listing_tile_mv. A V3Carousel mode=rail of photographed listings follows Atlas in the fold with price+address+beds/baths/sqft on 800x600 plates. The page still reads the recorded boundary itself because the LIST depends on its pins (Sunriver: 52 listings by polygon, 0 by subdivision name, measured 2026-09-09); the Atlas re-reads the resort outline on its own streamed budget so one miss is not both. Communities with no trusted polygon and no resort GeoJSON (sunriver, brasada-ranch) render the standin's unavailable state instead of nothing. Unknown type notFound().

The grok CLI and the Cursor CLI are missing in this sandbox, so the judge chain fell to its claude link (claude CLI, sonnet, subscription): three scorings of these shots in one call, recorded exactly as returned, no re-roll. Builder claude-opus-5.5 is not the judge.

First viewport, scale 1, palette-quantized, against this branch's own next build + next start.

tasteReview.beats: Redfin's Tetherow neighborhood page — this page wins on data depth (per-cluster median price pills tied to a live price-band slider, not just a pin drop) and on getting a buyer to a broker in one path, but Redfin still beats it on raw listing count density and saved-search tooling.

defects.finding: the median $1.4M, $1.4M, and $2.5M tags crowd into the same corner of the polygon at both 1440 and 375 and nearly overlap, so the map is unreadable exactly where the cheapest homes sit

defects.section: left rail below the price slider (desktop)
defects.finding: at 1440px the column under 'Up to any price' sits empty for roughly 400px before the listing dial begins, so the first fold reads unfinished instead of composed

the thumbnail strip under the big photo is a row of undifferentiated postage-stamp images with no visible price or spec distinction between them, functioning as a scroll list wearing thumbnails instead of a real filmstrip

tasteReview.verdict: This is the prescribed house kit (Atlas map, quiet claim line, listing dial) executed correctly and dully: the claim sentence is honest and sourced, the map is genuinely custom cartography with median pills rather than a raw Google map, and the dial's big serif '01/12' is the one moment with real personality. But the pills collide at the one cluster a buyer actually cares about, the desktop fold wastes a third of its width on empty space, and nothing here is a section a person would screenshot to show someone — it is competent, on-brand, and stops well short of breathtaking. demoMatch is true only because no catalog control was cream-boxed here; the house forms themselves just aren't earning the score their execution implies.
tasteReview.rebaselineReason: evaluatorModel grok-4.6 -> claude-sonnet-5; shotsHash (new captures of the listing dial, Matt 2026-09-24, SITE-195). The judge is a different instrument from the prior mark, so this is the first mark on the claude-sonnet-5 ruler for this class and the floor the next pass may not fall under.

contentFloor.note: No-regression floor (ci:route-content-floor). A build under any number here fails before the evaluator runs. Lower a number only by hand, in the same commit, with the reason. heroImageNatural LOWERED 2043 -> 576 (2026-09-21, PR #351 blocker): requiredComponents on this route carries no V3Stage/hero-photo primitive — the fold is Heading + claim, PlaceTypeAtlasSection (a map), then PlaceTypeFilm (a shadcn-carousel rail of magazine Cards). At seed time (2026-09-12) the widest inside the first 1200px was the site's own header logo (observed heroImageWidth 120 / heroImageNatural 2271 above is exactly logo-horizontal-navy-transparent.png's native width — a retina wordmark, not a photograph of Tetherow), because the Atlas pushed the carousel below 1200px on that render. It now sits inside 1200px, so PlaceTypeFilm's own Card photos (correctly requested at LISTING_FIELD_LEAD_PHOTO_SIZE, 800x600, via app/cities/[slug]/types/[type]/_v3/PlaceTypeFilm.client.tsx — never the banned 320x240 ledger thumb) win the widest-in-fold comparison instead, and their real delivered resolution is capped by Spark's per-photo derivative for the "ore" feed, not by our request. Verified 2026-09-21 directly against cdn.resize.sparkplatform.com at the same 800x600 bucket across 24 live MLS assets (including this route's own carousel assets 20260909222720819374000000 and 20260409235117531733000000, both measured at 720x480): real naturalWidth ranged 640-853px, never below 640, and a regression back to the banned 320x240 thumb would read exactly 320. 576 = floor(640 * 0.9), the same 0.9 TOLERANCE this gate applies everywhere else, applied to the true observed minimum for the correct/sanctioned photo size instead of to the unrelated logo asset. Floor-seeding artifact, not a quality regression: PlaceTypeFilm already requested the compliant size before and after this fix; only which element wins the "hero" comparison moved, and it moved to real inventory. heroImageNatural LOWERED 576 -> 420 (2026-09-23, PR #352): 576 assumed Spark never returns a lead photo under 640; CI run 35877907272 read 496 on /oregon/medford (a live listing's 800x600-bucket derivative). The floor exists to catch the banned 320x240 ledger thumb, which production /homes-for-sale?view=list served at 320 to 376 natural on 2026-09-23. Lead derivatives are now observed at 496 to 853. 420 sits between the two populations: a thumb still fails, a small lead does not. Set on all three classes whose winner is that same Spark lead bucket (oregon-city, place-type-community, price-drops).
